statement: The function returns a result r and r is true if and only if X = 0 or len(nums) is even, where X is the bitwise XOR of all elements of nums: X = nums[0] XOR nums[1] XOR ... XOR nums[len(nums)-1]. Thus r is exactly the truth value of Alice winning the chalkboard game under optimal play.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers satisfying 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] < 2^16 (65536).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and does not fail: there is no arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
